name: Refugi 307, Poble-sec (MUHBA)
story: Barcelona was bombed around 200 times during the war, mostly by Italian aircraft of the Aviazione Legionaria flying from Mallorca, with German participation. The residents of Poble-sec, a working-class district near the port and the Montjuïc gun batteries, dug this shelter themselves from 1937 under the Junta de Defensa Passiva. Its roughly 200 metres of narrow vaulted tunnels had water, a first-aid room, toilets, a fireplace and a children's area. Shelters like this saved many lives during the raids of 1938, including the three days of 16–18 March, when about 1,000 people were killed. After the war it was used to grow mushrooms and later as makeshift housing.
see: About 200 m of original galleries dug into the Montjuïc slope, with benches, the infirmary and toilets, and interpretation of civil defence in the city.
plan: Carrer Nou de la Rambla 175–179. Guided visits only, run by MUHBA (usually on Sunday mornings); book ahead online. Not suitable for claustrophobes.
